title: blockchain-detector-eval: when can you trust a blockchain anomaly detector, and what does it cost to run?

creators.name: Kuznetsov, Oleksandr
creators.affiliation: eCampus University, Novedrate (CO), Italy; V.N. Karazin Kharkiv National University, Kharkiv, Ukraine

description:
Evaluation code and results for blockchain anomaly detectors under realistic protocols: cross-chain bridge exploits (XChainWatcher), smart-contract vulnerability benchmarks (SmartBugs-curated, SolidiFI, DAppSCAN), temporal and address-disjoint evaluation on the Elliptic transaction graph, Kolmogorov–Arnold networks against same-size MLPs including LUT inference, and a keyword-selected cohort of flash-loan price-manipulation exploits on Ethereum (DeFiHackLabs, AWS public blockchain data). Every number comes from a numbered script and is stored with a manifest (code commit, input digests, package versions, configuration).

Licences: code MIT (LICENSE); documentation and result files CC BY 4.0 (results/LICENSE). Third-party datasets are not redistributed and keep their own terms (docs/DATA.md).
